Rules:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.

ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.

ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.

ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.

ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.

ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.

ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.

ID: RENEWAL
Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

ID: GOVLAW
Title: Governing law and venue
Kind: parametric
Summary: Accepted laws are New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales; courts, not foreign arbitration.

ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.

ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.

ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.

ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.

ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.

ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.

ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

plans.note: Section 15 is captioned as a one-way limitation of Garman's liability; review cap amount, mutuality and carve-outs (IP indemnity in sec-13, confidentiality in sec-14, gross negligence/wilful misconduct). Check interaction with warranty remedies in sec-12.

Section 13 provides an IP indemnity from Garman; confirm scope (defence, costs, no cap via sec-15) and add indemnity for Garman's own misconduct/personal injury/property damage. Verify no reciprocal broad customer indemnity.
No non-compete heading; software licence deals rarely contain one. Scan restrictions on use (sec-3) and general matters (sec-20) for any covenant limiting our use of competing routing products.
Likely absent, but check grant/restrictions (sec-2, sec-3) and maintenance/fees (sec-10, sec-11) for sole-source or exclusive-supplier language for support and future modules.
No pricing-parity heading; review fees (sec-11) and maintenance fee escalation (sec-10) for any obligation running against us, and note absence of an MFN in our favour as an optional ask.

Section 19 expressly binds employee non-solicitation; check mutuality, duration (target 12 months), scope limited to individuals involved in the project, and a general-advertising carve-out; also check survival treatment in sec-18.

Section 17 governs term and termination; confirm we may terminate maintenance/licence on notice without penalty and that Garman cannot terminate at convenience mid-term. Rejection rights in sec-7/sec-8 and maintenance term in sec-10 are related exit paths.
Auto-renewal of maintenance likely sits in sec-10 or sec-17; check notice window (target 30–60 days for us) and any uncapped renewal fee uplift in sec-11.

Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause should be in general matters (sec-20); confirm it is an accepted jurisdiction with courts rather than foreign arbitration, given the US/Canada-UK party mix.

Assignment clause expected in sec-20; secure affiliate/successor assignment and licence transfer rights (interacts with the grant in sec-2) and ensure no Garman termination right on our change of control (sec-17).

Ownership statements likely in the grant/restrictions (sec-2, sec-3); confirm our data (including converted data under sec-4) and any customisations we pay for are ours, that feedback/derivative clauses do not assign our IP, and align with confidentiality (sec-14) and escrow (sec-16).

Section 2 is the grant; check it is perpetual/irrevocable on payment, extends to affiliates and contractors, and that 'Authorized Locations' and other defined limits (sec-1, sec-6) plus sec-3 restrictions are not unduly narrow.

Any usage-verification right most likely accompanies the use restrictions in sec-3 or general matters (sec-20); require notice, business-hours, once-yearly, confidentiality-protected and vendor-cost audits.

Watch for interest on late payment, penalties or forfeiture of prepaid fees in sec-11, and any damages tied to our co-operation obligations in sec-9 or termination in sec-17; conversely note absence of service credits under sec-10.

Section 12 carries specifications and warranty; check duration runs from acceptance (sec-6), that the remedy is repair/replace with refund fallback, and that maintenance obligations (sec-10) do not displace the warranty; confirm no broad disclaimer.
No insurance heading; given on-site installation and training (sec-4, sec-5, sec-9), propose commercial general liability, professional liability/E&O and cyber cover in general matters (sec-20).

Check fees (sec-11) and maintenance (sec-10) for committed multi-year maintenance, minimum seat/location counts or non-refundable prepayments, and confirm an exit aligned with sec-17 termination rights.

Termination consequences in sec-17 (and sec-8 on rejection) likely address return of software but not our data or wind-down help; escrow (sec-16) is a partial substitute. Propose transition assistance and data return, with survival added in sec-18.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

paragraphs.text: 3. RESTRICTIONS ON USE
Sparkling shall:
(a) not copy the Software except to copy it onto another AS400 at the Authorized Locations and to make copies of the Software at each Authorized Location solely for backup purposes;
(b) not copy any of the Documentation except as required for Sparkling's internal purposes related to Sparkling's use of the Software;
(c) not assign this Agreement or transfer, lease, export or grant a sublicence of the Work to any Person, except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing;
(d) not reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble the Software;
(e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
(f) take all reasonable precautions to prevent third parties from using

the Work in any way that would constitute a breach of this Agreement including, without limitation, such precautions as Sparkling would otherwise take to protect its own proprietary software or hardware or information; and
10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, so we have replaced it with a mutual non-solicitation limited to individuals directly involved in the services, running 12 months from the end of their involvement, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. Our preferred position is no such restriction on us at all, but we are content with this narrowed mutual formulation.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.
Detection guidance:
"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

paragraphs.text: 10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. The existing Telephone support numbers are for Garman business hours 1-800-667-6901 or 1-306-242-6322

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

input.quote: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 19 binds us (mutually) with a no-hire, not merely a non-solicit: it prohibits hiring "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year, with no limitation to personnel involved in the services in its first limb and no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions covering all of the counterparty's personnel are a walk-away under the playbook. Since the restriction is mutual and part of the existing bargain, we narrow to the fallback rather than delete: a 12-month non-solicit running from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited. Survival in Section 18 remains acceptable for the narrowed clause.

proposal.summary: Convert mutual no-hire into a narrow 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, so we have replaced it with a mutual non-solicitation limited to individuals directly involved in the services, running 12 months from the end of their involvement, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. Our preferred position is no such restriction on us at all, but we are content with this narrowed mutual formulation.

Since the restriction is mutual and part of the existing bargain, we narrow to the fallback rather than delete: a 12-month non-solicit running from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited. Survival in Section 18 remains acceptable for the narrowed clause.

proposal.summary: Convert mutual no-hire into a narrow 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, so we have replaced it with a mutual non-solicitation limited to individuals directly involved in the services, running 12 months from the end of their involvement, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. Our preferred position is no such restriction on us at all, but we are content with this narrowed mutual formulation.

Rule:
ID: NOSOLICIT
Title: Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We accept only narrow, time-limited non-solicits with a general-advertising carve-out.
Severity: medium
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-solicit on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Position — walk-away:
No-hire provisions, or restrictions longer than 24 months or covering all Vendor personnel.

"shall not solicit", "employ or engage", "no-hire", "induce … to leave". Determine duration, scope (all employees vs those involved) and whether a general-solicitation carve-out exists.

Redline guidance:
Narrow to the fallback with minimal edits (duration, scope, carve-out sentence). Delete any no-hire.

Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, restrictive covenants).**

Section 19 imposes a mutual **no-hire** — not a non-solicit — barring either party (and its affiliates) from hiring "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year, with no involvement-based limitation in its first limb and no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. That is a playbook walk-away as drafted, and it binds Sparkling Spring Water Group.

Because the restriction is mutual and already part of the bargain, I redlined to the fallback rather than deleting Section 19: a 12-month non-solicit measured from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited and carve-outs for general recruitment and unsolicited approaches. Survival under Section 18 remains acceptable for the narrowed clause.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: NONCOMPETE
Title: Non-compete restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not accept restrictions on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Restriction limited to a named competing product, during the term only, capped at 12 months, with a carve-out for internal development and acquisitions.

Position — walk-away:
Post-term non-compete longer than 12 months, or undefined scope ("any competing business").
Detection guidance:
Look for "shall not … develop/market/sell/engage in", "competing products", "compete with Vendor", field-of-use or territory restrictions binding Customer. Restrictions binding the Vendor are fine.

Redline guidance:
Delete the restriction on Customer; if the vendor relationship plausibly needs protection, narrow to the fallback. Comment: we cannot restrict our business; offer the narrowed fallback.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.

Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the \"Losses\") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 contains a Garman indemnity, but it is limited to breach of the IP ownership/non-infringement warranty and provides no express duty to defend, no coverage for Sparkling's affiliates, and nothing for Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling data, or Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct (including resulting personal injury or property damage). There is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity, and Section 15 already carves Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the cap is not an issue. The inserted paragraph adds the missing indemnity heads and standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics, reaching the preferred position with a minimal addition to the existing section.

ops.text: In addition, Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates from and against any third party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Work, or any Improvements or Modifications thereto, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) Garman's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sparkling's data or Confidential Information caused by Garman; or (d) Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, including any resulting personal injury, death or damage to tangible property. Sparkling shall give Garman prompt written notice of any such claim, Garman shall have control of its defence and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or admission on Sparkling shall be made without Sparkling's prior written consent), and Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation at Garman's expense.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives us an infringement remedy tied to a warranty breach but no express duty to defend and nothing for Garman's own misconduct, so we have added a defence and indemnity obligation covering IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. If needed, we can accept customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations or specifications) and a refund remedy as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Garman defence/indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard claim procedure.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

Rule:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).

MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.

Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.

Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity obligation in either direction. Targeted searches ("no less favourable", "favourable/favorable", "price", "customers", "third part") surfaced nothing relevant, and the candidate sections confirm this:

- **§11 Fees (p0084)** — a bare obligation to pay per the Fee Schedule; no parity or price-matching commitment.
- **§10 Maintenance and Support (p0065–p0082)** — Garman-side service obligations plus limited chargeable-repair carve-outs; no fee-parity or benchmarking language.
- **§20 General Matters (p0141–p0147)** — standard boilerplate (waiver, assignment, independent contractors, force majeure, severability, governing law); no MFN.

Since nothing requires Sparkling to offer Garman terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, the preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer) is satisfied. An MFN in our favour would be welcome but is an optional ask only, so no redline was raised.

Title: Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window
Kind: parametric
Summary: Renewals must be easy to exit and priced predictably.

Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.

Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) is limited to ordinary licence-scope restrictions on the Software and Documentation (no copying beyond backup, no reverse engineering, no sublicence/assignment, no service bureau use of the Work); none of these limit the businesses Sparkling may operate or the routing products it may buy or build. Section 19 is a mutual non-solicitation of employees (one year, both parties), not a non-compete, and Section 20 (General Matters) contains only boilerplate. Text searches for "compet", "develop" and "exclusiv" surface no competing-products, territory or field-of-use restriction on our party. Consistent with the playbook preferred position, no redline is required.

input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation
input.rationale: Section 13 contains a Garman indemnity, but it is limited to breach of the IP ownership/non-infringement warranty and provides no express duty to defend, no coverage for Sparkling's affiliates, and nothing for Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling data, or Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct (including resulting personal injury or property damage). There is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity, and Section 15 already carves Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the cap is not an issue. The inserted paragraph adds the missing indemnity heads and standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics, reaching the preferred position with a minimal addition to the existing section.

ops.text: In addition, Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates from and against any third party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Work, or any Improvements or Modifications thereto, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) Garman's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sparkling's data or Confidential Information caused by Garman; or (d) Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, including any resulting personal injury, death or damage to tangible property. Sparkling shall give Garman prompt written notice of any such claim, Garman shall have control of its defence and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or admission on Sparkling shall be made without Sparkling's prior written consent), and Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation at Garman's expense.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives us an infringement remedy tied to a warranty breach but no express duty to defend and nothing for Garman's own misconduct, so we have added a defence and indemnity obligation covering IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. If needed, we can accept customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations or specifications) and a refund remedy as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Garman defence/indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard claim procedure.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

10. MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT

For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
(a) SOFTWARE UPDATE SERVICE
As part of the Software Update Service, Garman shall provide to Sparkling as soon as reasonably available:
(1) corrections and bug fixes for the Software;
(2) all modifications, refinements, and enhancements ("Improvements") of the Software;
(3) new releases of the Software; and
(4) updated user manuals to support all of the above in a reasonable time frame.
(b) TELEPHONE SUPPORT SERVICE

Telephone Support Service includes Sparkling having direct telephone access to employees of Garman who have the necessary technical expertise and experience to understand and consider Sparkling's inquiries concerning the failure of Software to operate according to Specifications and to clarify Documentation that is either insufficient or unclear. Such direct telephone access shall be available in accordance with the Telephone Support Schedule. In the event that the Telephone Support Service does provide a resolution to Sparkling (acting reasonably) within 2 business days to permit the Software to meet the Specifications, then Garman shall provide Software Repair Services to address the Software failure. Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:

"automatically renew", "unless either party gives notice … days prior", renewal term length, price uplift language. Compute the notice window in days and the renewal term length.

Shorten the notice window (≤ 30, fallback ≤ 60 days), set renewal term to 12 months, cap uplift.

Rule:
ID: EXCLUSIVITY
Title: Exclusivity obligations binding Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers.
Severity: high
Category: restrictive-covenants
Position — preferred:
No exclusivity or "sole supplier" obligation on Customer.
Position — fallback:
Exclusivity limited to a defined product category and 12 months, ending automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

Position — walk-away:
Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit.

Phrases like "exclusive", "sole and exclusive provider", "shall purchase all of its requirements from", "shall not procure … from any third party". Exclusivity granted to Customer (e.g. Vendor won't serve our competitors) is acceptable and not a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback; keep any exclusivity that benefits Customer.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN, critical).**

- **What exists:** Section 13 (p0090–p0093) contains a Garman warranty of IP ownership/non-infringement plus an indemnity for Losses arising from breach of that warranty, with procure/modify/replace remedies. Section 15 (p0105) helpfully carves Sections 13 and 14 out of the liability limitation, so the indemnity is uncapped. No reciprocal Sparkling indemnity appears anywhere in the document.
- **Gap vs. preferred position:** no express duty to **defend**, no coverage of Sparkling's **affiliates**, and no indemnity for Garman's **breach of applicable law**, **unauthorized access to/disclosure of Sparkling data**, or **gross negligence/wilful misconduct** (including resulting personal injury or property damage). Standard claim mechanics (notice, control, cooperation) are also absent for those heads.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** a single new paragraph inserted after p0093 in Section 13 adding Garman's defend-and-indemnify obligation across the four heads with standard notice/control/cooperation, keeping the edit minimal and inside the existing uncapped section.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (LOL-CAP, critical)** — §15 (p0104–p0105).

- **What's wrong:** No aggregate liability cap exists at all; the section only excludes indirect/consequential damages and declares direct damages the exclusive remedy. The caption is one-sided ("Limitation of Garman's Liability"), and the carve-out covers only breaches of Sections 13 and 14 — nothing express for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, data protection/security or IP infringement, and Sparkling's fee obligations are not excluded from the cap.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** heading made mutual, and a mutual cap added at the greater of (a) 12 months' fees paid or payable by Sparkling and (b) USD 1,000,000, with an "Excluded Claims" definition that preserves the Section 13/14 carve-out and puts indemnification, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap; fee payments are not treated as capped damages.
- **Fallback if pushed:** plain mutual 12 months' fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
