content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity, licence scope) — §2 Grant of License (p0028)**

- **Compliant aspects:** the grant already extends to Sparkling's affiliated companies operating at Authorized Locations, and §17(a) makes it perpetual so long as fees are paid, with §17(c) converting it to a fee-free perpetual licence on Garman's default — so it is not revocable at Garman's discretion.
- **Gaps:** (i) contractors acting on our behalf are not covered (and §3(g) only carves out affiliates); (ii) the licence is expressly "non-transferable", reinforced by §3(c) and §20(d) which require Garman's consent for any assignment or transfer, so the licence would not follow our business in an M&A transaction.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** insert contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf into the grant and delete "non-transferable", replacing it with a right to transfer to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, notwithstanding §§3(c) and 20(d). Fallback offered in the comment: affiliates/contractors added on written notice.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant (no redline proposed).**

The agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection or usage-verification right against Sparkling:

- **Section 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the natural location for a usage-verification right — contains only substantive covenants (no copying, no reverse engineering, no sublicensing) with no inspection, reporting or system-access mechanism.
- **Section 20 (General Matters)** covers only time-of-essence and notices; **Section 14 (Confidentiality)** is mutual and contains no access-for-verification right.
- Full-text searches for *audit*, *inspect*, *verify*, *examine*, *records*, *premises*, *monitor* and *compliance* surface nothing binding on us. The single examination right in the document (escrow materials, p0114) runs in **our** favour, letting Sparkling retain independent experts to test Garman's deposited materials.
- The only termination-related obligation is a self-certification of deletion (p0118), which is not an audit right.

Since the playbook position is a *cap* on vendor audits, their complete absence is better than the preferred position. Proposing frequency/notice/cost limits would gratuitously create an audit right Garman does not have, so we should leave this alone. If Garman later requests verification language in negotiation, we would hold to the preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.

paragraphs.text: 17. TERM AND TERMINATION

(a) This Agreement and the license granted under this Agreement shall remain in effect perpetually as long as fees are paid by Sparkling in accordance with the Fee Schedule and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated in accordance with this Section.

(b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
(c) If either party:
(1) makes an assignment in bankruptcy or is adjudicated a bankrupt;
(2) makes a general assignment for the benefit of its creditors;

(3) has a receiver, administrator or manager of its property, assets or undertaking appointed in such circumstances as would in the reasonable discretion of the other party, detrimentally affect such other party's rights under this Agreement;

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

ID: LD
Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: Service credits to us are welcome; liquidated damages against us are not.
Severity: high
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
Position — walk-away:
Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Identify liquidated damages, penalties, minimum fees on termination, "shall pay … as liquidated damages". Flag only when Customer pays. Service credits or LDs payable by Vendor to Customer are compliant.

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

(4) the Software being transferred to a different networking environment or hardware configuration without the prior written consent of Garman; or

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.comment: [Playbook] Garman installs and maintains the Software at our Authorized Locations and converts our data, so we need it to carry standard cover. We have added a short insurance covenant (commercial general liability USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, plus statutory workers' compensation and certificates on request); we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: (k) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where Garman processes Sparkling's data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide Sparkling with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage on request.

content.text: No customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or minimum/early-termination fees appear anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, forfeiture or minimum-fee provision payable by Sparkling (the customer). Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay fees per the Fee Schedule; there is no late-payment interest or penalty. Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination fee or accelerated/remaining-term payment, and Section 17 default termination by Sparkling actually converts the licence to perpetual and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees for services not rendered. Sections 3, 9 and 19 impose no monetary penalties on Sparkling. Section 15 confirms each party's remedy is direct damages only, excluding consequential loss. Any LD-type amounts run in our favour, which the playbook treats as compliant, so no redline is required.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: missing (insurance clause absent)** — severity low, confidence 0.85.

- The Agreement has no insurance provision at all; a document-wide search for "insurance" returns no hits, and there is no insurance heading in the section outline.
- Insurance is nonetheless warranted: Garman installs the Software on Sparkling's AS400s at the Authorized Locations (§ 4(a)), performs future installations and conversions of Sparkling's data (§ 4(b)), and delivers on-site training and maintenance — i.e., a vendor that both touches our premises and processes our data.
- Redline (validated, ok:true): insert a new § 20(k) in General Matters, immediately after the entire-agreement subsection (p0149), requiring Garman to carry CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M where it processes Sparkling's data, statutory workers' compensation, and to furnish certificates on request, for the term plus one year.
- Fallback flagged in the comment: E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties, forfeitures, or minimum/early-termination fees on Sparkling (our side):

- **§ 11 (Fees)** — bare obligation to pay per the Fee Schedule; no late-payment interest or penalty mechanic.
- **§ 17(b) (Termination)** — we may terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with **no** termination fee, accelerated fees, or payment of remaining contract value.
- **§ 17 (default)** — on Garman's default, the licence converts to perpetual and fee-free and Garman must refund prepaid fees for services not rendered (i.e., LD-type value runs in our favour, which the playbook treats as acceptable).
- **§§ 3, 9, 19** — use restrictions, co-operation, and non-solicitation carry no monetary penalties.
- **§ 15** — mutual remedy is limited to direct damages, with consequential loss excluded.

One note for negotiation, not a rule breach: § 10 (Maintenance and Support) contains no service credit regime, so we have no pre-agreed remedy for support failures. That falls outside this rule (which only bites where the customer pays), but may be worth raising under the service levels rule.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: The Software conformance warranty period (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, extended while maintenance continues) meets the preferred 12-month position, and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer or "AS IS" language anywhere in the agreement, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty (Section 15 limits damages only). However, the warranty is incomplete: (i) no remedy is attached to it — repair is available only as a Maintenance Service under Section 10 (p0077), which is fee-bearing and could lapse, and the Section 7/8 refund is confined to the acceptance period; (ii) there is no professional and workmanlike warranty covering installation, data conversion, training and maintenance services; and (iii) there are no malicious code or legal compliance warranties. We therefore insert a single paragraph in Section 12 adding the services warranty, malicious code/compliance warranties and a repair/replace-then-refund remedy, and confirming the warranty is not displaced by Section 10 maintenance.

ops.text: Garman further warrants that (a) all services provided under this Agreement, including installation, data conversion, training and Maintenance Services, shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) the Software and such services shall comply with all applicable laws; and (c) the Software shall not contain any virus, disabling device or other malicious code. Sparkling's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 12 shall be, at Garman's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Software or services at no charge to Sparkling, and if Garman fails to do so within 30 business days of written notice, a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Software or services. The warranties in this Section 12 are in addition to, and not limited or displaced by, the Maintenance Services described in Section 10.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 12 gives a one-year Software conformance warranty but no stated warranty remedy, no services warranty and no malicious-code or legal-compliance warranty, and repair is currently available only under the paid maintenance arrangement in Section 10. We have added a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus a repair/replace-then-refund remedy, consistent with our standard warranty position; if helpful we can accept a 90-day services warranty period.
proposal.summary: Add services warranty, malicious code and legal compliance warranties, and an express repair/replace/refund remedy to Section 12.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position. Use fallback only when the rule guidance or existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 14. CONFIDENTIALITY

By virtue of this Agreement, the parties may have access to information that is confidential to one another ("Confidential Information"). Confidential Information means all data and information related to the business and management of either party, including proprietary and trade secrets, technology and accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement, provided that such Confidential Information shall not include data or information which:
(a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the other party;
(b) is already in the rightful possession of the other party prior to its receipt from the other party;
(c) is independently developed by the other party;
(d) is lawfully obtained by the other party from a third party;
(e) is disclosed as required by law; or
(f) is disclosed to professional advisors in confidence.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent Sparkling Spring Water Group Limited; counterparty is Garman Routing Systems, Inc..

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (medium) — Section 12 (Specifications and Warranty)**

**What the document does well:** the Software conformance warranty runs for one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and continues while maintenance is in place, which meets our preferred 12-month software position. There is no "AS IS" clause and no disclaimer of implied warranties anywhere in the agreement, so the express warranty is not swallowed; Section 15 limits damage types only.

**Gaps identified:**
1. **No warranty remedy.** Repair exists only as a fee-bearing Maintenance Service (Section 10(c), p0077), and the refund path in Sections 7–8 is confined to the acceptance period. If maintenance lapses, the warranty has no teeth.
2. **No services warranty.** Installation, data conversion, training and maintenance are all performed by Garman with no professional/workmanlike standard.
3. **No malicious code or legal compliance warranties.**

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** a single inserted paragraph in Section 12 adding the professional and workmanlike services warranty, compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties, an at-Garman's-option re-performance/repair/replace remedy with a refund backstop if uncured within 30 business days, and a confirmation that the warranty is not displaced by Section 10 maintenance. The comment offers a 90-day services warranty as the fallback.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-commitment language. Fees are payable only "as set out in the Fee Schedule" for the licensed Software and Authorized Locations actually taken (§ 11, § 2), and maintenance runs on a "renewable one-year term" (§ 10) rather than a multi-year committed spend. Sparkling also has an at-will exit on 90 days' notice under § 17(b), and the license continues only "as long as fees are paid", so there is no locked-in spend. The § 3 restrictions are ordinary IP/scope-of-use limits, not volume caps or purchase obligations. This meets the preferred position (usage/ordered services only); no redline required. Note only that the Fee Schedule (Schedule "A") is not included in the reviewed text and should be checked to confirm it contains no minimum quantities or non-refundable multi-year prepayments.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-commitment language. Fees are payable only "as set out in the Fee Schedule" for the licensed Software and Authorized Locations actually taken (§ 11, § 2), and maintenance runs on a "renewable one-year term" (§ 10) rather than a multi-year committed spend. Sparkling also has an at-will exit on 90 days' notice under § 17(b), and the license continues only "as long as fees are paid", so there is no locked-in spend. The § 3 restrictions are ordinary IP/scope-of-use limits, not volume caps or purchase obligations. This meets the preferred position (usage/ordered services only); no redline required. Note only that the Fee Schedule (Schedule "A") is not included in the reviewed text and should be checked to confirm it contains no minimum quantities or non-refundable multi-year prepayments.

input.rationale: Section 17 addresses only Sparkling's obligations to stop using and return Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes; there is no reciprocal obligation on Garman to provide transition assistance, return Sparkling's data (converted and hosted under Section 4/Schedule D) in a usable format, or certify deletion. The only data-return language is in Section 8, which applies solely if Sparkling rejects the Software during acceptance, and the escrow in Section 16 is at most a partial substitute. We therefore insert a new Section 17(d) with six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, a 30-day machine-readable data return and post-return deletion certification, and add it to the Section 18 survival list so it operates after termination.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (1) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (2) within thirty (30) calendar days of Sparkling's request, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in its possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (3) thereafter delete Sparkling's data from its systems and certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing.

**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment on Sparkling:

- **§ 11 (Fees)** — payment is limited to "the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule," with no committed volume or spend.
- **§ 2 (Grant of License)** — additional fees arise only if Sparkling elects to use the Software beyond the Authorized Locations, i.e., ordered items only.
- **§ 10 (Maintenance)** — a "renewable one-year term," not a multi-year committed maintenance stream.
- **§ 17(a)–(b)** — the license runs perpetually "as long as fees are paid," and Sparkling may terminate at any time on 90 days' notice, giving a clean exit.
- **§ 3** — restrictions are conventional IP/scope-of-use limits (copying, reverse engineering, assignment), not volume caps on our usage.

This satisfies the preferred position, so no edit is warranted. One diligence point flagged in the finding: Schedule "A" (Fee Schedule) is referenced but not included in the reviewed text, and should be checked for minimum quantities, seat/location floors, or non-refundable multi-year prepayments before signature.

**Finding: missing (medium severity) — no post-termination transition assistance or data return.**

What I found:
- **Section 17 (Term and Termination)** imposes exit obligations only on us: on our 90-day termination we must cease use and certify destruction/return of Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes (p0118). Garman has no reciprocal wind-down duty; p0128–p0129 only convert the licence and refund prepaid fees on Garman default.
- **Section 8** does require Garman to return our Confidential Information, but only in the narrow scenario where we reject the Software during acceptance testing — not on ordinary expiry or termination.
- **Section 16 (source code escrow)** is at best a partial substitute, and **Section 14** contains no return-on-termination mechanic. Meanwhile Section 4/Schedule D has Garman converting and handling our data, so the gap is material.

Redline (validated, ok:true):
1. New **Section 17(d)** inserted after p0129: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at Garman's then-current rates on request; return of all Sparkling data within thirty (30) days in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and deletion thereafter with written certification.
2. **Section 18** survival list updated to include 17(d) so the obligation is enforceable after termination.

Fallback flagged in the comment: 90 days of transition assistance, provided the 30-day machine-readable export is preserved. Walk-away would be no data return or immediate deletion on termination.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Sparkling, the Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review — Software License and Maintenance Agreement  

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **18 findings: 3 critical, 6 high, 8 medium and 1 low**. Of these, **9 are deviations**, **3 are missing terms** and **6 are already compliant**.

The three critical items sit in the ri[REDACTED] core of the deal. **Section 15** contains no aggregate liability cap at all and is drafted as a limitation of Garman's liability only, without express uncapped carve-outs for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, data protection/security or IP infringement. **Section 13** gives us a narrow IP indemnity tied only to the ownership/non-infringement warranty, with no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage and nothing for breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. The same section vests ownership of all IP in the Work — including the Schedule "D" Modifications we paid for — in Garman, with a sweep-up broad enough to capture our own inputs and data.

At the high level, the assignment regime (Section 20(d), reinforced by Section 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in Section 2) imposes blanket consent with no affiliate or M&A carve-out for us, which is a walk-away position and also undermines the licence grant on a corporate transaction. Our convenience right under Section 17(b) works but runs on 90 days' notice with no refund of prepaid maintenance fees.

Medium items are largely gap-filling: Nova Scotia governing law and non-exclusive jurisdiction fall outside our accepted list; maintenance renewal mechanics and renewal-fee protection are absent; there is no Garman-side transition assistance or return/deletion of our data on termination; the Section 12 warranty carries no remedy and no services, malicious code or compliance warranties; and Section 19 is a mutual **no-hire** rather than a non-solicit. There is no insurance clause anywhere in the Agreement.

Helpfully, the Agreement is clean on several fronts we often have to fight: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, no non-compete or field-of-use covenant, no vendor audit right against our usage, no MFN and no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment.

*Note: automated verification was skipped for all findings below; each rests on the reviewer's rationale as recorded.*

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 |
| 11 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Missing | § 10 Maintenance and Support |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use |
| 16 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 17 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 11 Fees |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 11 |

### Positions taken on the deviations and gaps

- **§ 13 (indemnity):** we add a Garman defence and indemnity for IP infringement, breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Sparkling data, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. Section 15 already carves Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the cap is not an obstacle here.
- **§ 13 (IP ownership):** we take the playbook fallback given the object-code/escrow bargain — Garman keeps its platform IP, our data and supplied materials are carved out, we take a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Modifications and Improvements we pay for, and joint ownership is excluded.
- **§ 15:** we add a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, an Excluded Claims definition (preserving the existing Section 13/14 carve-out), exclusion of our payment obligations from the cap, and a mutual heading. Fallback: a plain mutual 12 months' fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
- **§ 20(d) / § 3(c) / § 2:** affiliate and successor assignment carve-out for us; Garman's assignment subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and not to our competitors; confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and triggers no termination or re-pricing right.
- **§ 2:** extend the licence to contractors acting on our behalf and permit transfer to a successor.
- **§ 17(b):** 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Fallback: 60 days, provided the refund is preserved.
- **Governing law:** New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. There is no arbitration clause, so only the jurisdiction words and forum change.
- **§ 19:** narrow to a 12-month mutual non-solicit running from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited. Survival under Section 18 remains acceptable for the narrowed clause.
- **§ 12:** add a professional and workmanlike services warranty (installation, data conversion, training, maintenance), malicious code and legal compliance warranties, and a repair/replace-then-refund remedy, confirming the warranty is not displaced by fee-bearing Section 10 maintenance.
- **§ 10:** add 12-month renewal terms we may decline on 30 days' notice, a 60-day Garman reminder, and a cap on renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3%. Fallback: 60-day window and 5% cap.
- **New § 17(d):** six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable form within 30 days and post-return deletion certification, added to the Section 18 survival list.
- **New § 20(k):** short vendor insurance covenant in General Matters, after the entire-agreement subsection.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings engage express playbook walk-away positions:

1. **Assignment — blanket consent with no affiliate or M&A carve-out (Section 20(d), reinforced by Section 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in Section 2).** A consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no carve-out for our affiliates or successors is our walk-away position; combined with the licence terms it would leave the licence unusable on a corporate transaction.
2. **Section 19 — mutual no-hire covering "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year.** No-hire provisions covering all of the counterparty's personnel are a walk-away. Because the restriction is mutual and part of the existing bargain, we propose narrowing to the fallback non-solicit rather than deletion.

We also flag the three critical items (Sections 13 and 15) as must-fix: an unlimited, one-sided liability regime combined with a narrow indemnity and Garman ownership of the Modifications we paid for is not a package we can recommend signing as drafted.

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook and identified **18 findings: 3 critical, 6 high, 8 medium and 1 low**. Of these, **9 are deviations**, **3 are missing terms** and **6 are already compliant**.

The three critical items sit in the ri[REDACTED] core of the deal. **Section 15** contains no aggregate liability cap at all and is drafted as a limitation of Garman's liability only, without express uncapped carve-outs for gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, data protection/security or IP infringement. **Section 13** gives us a narrow IP indemnity tied only to the ownership/non-infringement warranty, with no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage and nothing for breach of law, data incidents or gross negligence/wilful misconduct. The same section vests ownership of all IP in the Work — including the Schedule "D" Modifications we paid for — in Garman, with a sweep-up broad enough to capture our own inputs and data.

At the high level, the assignment regime (Section 20(d), reinforced by Section 3(c) and the "non-transferable" grant in Section 2) imposes blanket consent with no affiliate or M&A carve-out for us, which is a walk-away position and also undermines the licence grant on a corporate transaction. Our convenience right under Section 17(b) works but runs on 90 days' notice with no refund of prepaid maintenance fees.

Medium items are largely gap-filling: Nova Scotia governing law and non-exclusive jurisdiction fall outside our accepted list; maintenance renewal mechanics and renewal-fee protection are absent; there is no Garman-side transition assistance or return/deletion of our data on termination; the Section 12 warranty carries no remedy and no services, malicious code or compliance warranties; and Section 19 is a mutual **no-hire** rather than a non-solicit. There is no insurance clause anywhere in the Agreement.

Helpfully, the Agreement is clean on several fronts we often have to fight: no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation, no liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, no non-compete or field-of-use covenant, no vendor audit right against our usage, no MFN and no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment.
